method.scope: private monophonic transcription only; no public API, shared provider, pYIN decoder, persisted format, or polyphonic algorithm change
method.diagnosis: On controlled 110 Hz repeats, voiced pitch tracking remains accurate and continuous but two-period RMS averaging blurs the attack/release valleys. The failure is segmentation, not a missed pitch.
method.candidate: Preserve legacy two-period cuts; add narrow one-period valleys below 0.5 of the quieter local crest; shallower valleys below the existing 0.7 width ratio require normalized spectral-flux support within 50 ms.
method.normalization: Use finite positive original extracted-note peak RMS values; select the descending rank min(3, count/4), and invert that reference. At or below the existing minus 80 dB floor, or with invalid normalization, disable shallow support. Audio, pitch analysis, and velocity remain unscaled.
method.selection: Legacy cuts precede deep additions, then supported shallow additions. Enforce frame deduplication and minimum duration against both neighbors. One spectral onset supports at most one accepted shallow cut. Commit cue use only after child construction succeeds; otherwise rebuild the legacy children before falling back to the parent.
method.cost: One prefix sum per parent, reused for both RMS windows. Normalized onset analysis is lazy and runs at most once per transcription; no full spectrogram or waveform copy.

sources.title: Maximum Filter Vibrato Suppression for Onset Detection

method.attribution: The RMS supplement and body-level normalization are local design choices; paper results are not accuracy claims for this candidate.

protocol.conditions: All twelve pooled note/offset F comparisons and twelve TP comparisons must be nondecreasing on the six observed reference groups. Synthetic targets and unchanged regressions pass; raw onset oracle remains exact. Only after passing observed data and cost review may the selected new confirmation be exposed.

scoring.audio: native 44100 Hz, no resampling, normalization, cropping or alignment fitting; fixed gain control separately scales float samples by 0.1 without re-quantization

correction_before_recorded_predictions.reason: The initial design assumed a new 110 Hz, 75-cent, 6 Hz vibrato control was one note in the adopted baseline. Baseline itself splits it into two at all four rates. The whole family was moved to truthful characterization before recorded predictions, with no additional candidate deterioration allowed.

vocalset.status: all observed before this candidate; not a new holdout
vocalset.pitch_reference: human-reviewed Sound-interval median F0 from pYIN-assisted contours; not independent frame-F0 truth

gain.status: derived from observed Vocadito development recordings; not additional independent recordings

extra_prediction.branch: one-period shallow valley plus normalized spectral support
extra_prediction.reference: both annotation conventions describe one note across this region
extra_prediction.conclusion: A brief amplitude dip followed by spectral recovery can occur within a sustained note. The two features are insufficient evidence of a new note.

other_changed_recording.interpretation: separate duration change; do not attribute the net extra prediction to this recording

follow_up_hypothesis.condition: Require the RMS support interval to overlap one of the two finite STFT windows used for the supporting novelty frame.
follow_up_hypothesis.result: Rejected as a remedy for this false split: the previous STFT window overlaps by 26 samples (about 0.590 ms), so the necessary overlap condition still admits it.
follow_up_hypothesis.meaning: Finite support overlap is not sufficient to establish that both cues describe a separate note. No fitted overlap length or shorter association radius was introduced.

validation.before_fix: four repeated target notes are detected as one
validation.gain_checks: High-gain 0.18 targets scaled by 1, 0.1, 0.01 as floats; corresponding counts/MIDI, endpoint-within-hop, pitch-within-cent and normalized-frame equality checks pass above the existing gate floor.
validation.independent_code_review: passed after adding a right-neighbor-only counterexample and exercising the actual shared fallback/cue-commit path

low_register.format: float32 WAV, known sample-aligned note events

fast_am.interpretation: intended single held note with amplitude modulation; characterize errors against that truth, not as a passing assertion

confirmation.status: retained unpredicted because observed acceptance failed; do not imply this candidate passed confirmation
confirmation.relationship: singer-disjoint within VocalSet; cross-corpus identity overlap is unknown

performance.reason: Observed acceptance failed before the six-run cost and confirmation phases; no performance claim for this candidate.

reproduction.patch_base: the adopted source hashes in protocol.baseline_source_sha256; includes the earlier acoustic-boundary improvement

limitations: The default transcriber retains its earlier short low-note limitation because this candidate was rejected.
The 110 Hz wide-vibrato and fast-AM errors already exist in the baseline and are not claimed solved.
The lower-register characterization improves 16/64 to 56/64 note matches but still misses eight notes; these are generated signals.
The recorded-corpus gains do not override the fixed per-reference acceptance failures.
No frame-level F0 improvement or broad instrument generalization is established.
